anchors_0_to_4: Questioning is dominated by leading, compound or closed questions and refers to the subject's demeanor ("You seem nervous...").
Three kinds of lapse; the interview leans on closed and leading questions.
Two kinds of lapse, for example several closed questions and one leading question.
One kind of lapse, for example one compound question in an otherwise clean, open interview.
Every question is a single neutral ask; most invite a narrative ("Walk me through...", "What task required entry?"); nothing suggests an answer or comments on how the subject sounds.
dimensions.name: clarity and neutrality

subchecks.text: No leading or suggestive question. No question presupposes a contested fact or signals the wanted answer.
Open or probing share. At least 60% of questions are typed open or probing.
No poorly framed question. No question is compound, has an ambiguous referent, a double negative or undefined jargon; **and** no question's answer is labeled PFQ (automatic fail, S3-D4).
No loaded or demeanor wording. No hostile or loaded wording; no reference to nervousness, demeanor, accent, fluency, appearance or tone.

anchors_0_to_4: No visible connection between answers and the next question, or questions drift from the objective.
Mostly ignores answers; repeats demands the subject has said they cannot meet.
Questions often read like a prepared list that ignores what was just said.
Tracks answers well with one lapse, for example lets one evasive answer pass.
Each question picks up the last answer; a non-answer is met with a neutral rephrase of the same ask; "I don't know" is accepted or helped with a cue, not hammered.
dimensions.name: response relevance

subchecks.na_when: N/A unless an answer is labeled EVA
subchecks.text: Presses evasion. N/A unless an answer is labeled EVA. Every EVA answer is followed within the next two questions by a question that asks again for the withheld fact in different, neutral words.

subchecks.na_when: N/A unless an answer is labeled UNC
subchecks.text: Respects uncertainty. N/A unless an answer is labeled UNC. No later question demands the same unknown fact again without a new retrieval cue or new evidence.
On objective. Every question concerns the investigation objective or something the subject or a released record introduced.
Builds on answers. At least half of the questions after the first build on content in the immediately preceding answer.

anchors_0_to_4: No question uses the answers' content or the records.
Little use of evidence; records are read out as accusations.
Uses evidence sometimes; discloses a record before asking for the account, or asks only general questions.
Evidence-led with one omission, for example a contradiction left unraised.
Names what is missing, asks for checkable specifics, lets the subject commit to an account before showing a record, and puts every inconsistency to the subject neutrally.
dimensions.name: evidence-based follow-up

subchecks.text: Names the gap. At least one question asks for a specific fact an earlier answer left missing (the EX-2 pattern).
Checkable detail. At least one question asks for an unanticipated, verifiable detail: time, sequence, layout, named person or document.

subchecks.na_when: N/A unless a record is released before the last question
subchecks.text: Uses released records. N/A unless a record is released before the last question. Each released record is followed within the next three questions by a question on the point it bears on.

subchecks.na_when: N/A unless a question discloses a record's content
subchecks.text: Account before disclosure. N/A unless a question discloses a record's content. Before each such question, an earlier question asked for the subject's own account of the same point.

subchecks.na_when: N/A unless R1 (or R3's R1-mode call) reports a contradiction trigger (1.3.2) before the last question (for a turn-document pair, both the turn and the document's availability: exchange 0 for an initial document, its release for a record)
subchecks.text: Raises contradictions. Each reported visible contradiction (two subject turns R1 lists as a conflicting pair, or a statement that conflicts on its face with an initial document or a released record) is raised by a later neutral question; a contradiction of a hidden canonical fact is not something the investigator can see and never makes 3e applicable (SG2-37).

anchors_0_to_4: Confession-seeking: every question presupposes the violation.
Treats one reading as settled for most of the interview.
Asks for explanations but never checks them, or checks them while presupposing guilt.
Tests alternatives with one lapse, for example one presupposing question.
Treats the after-hours entry as unexplained, asks the subject to explain it, then asks which panel they touched, a detail that differs between the two accounts.
dimensions.name: testing alternative explanations

subchecks.text: Invites explanation. At least one question openly invites the subject to explain a circumstance that could look suspicious.

subchecks.na_when: N/A unless a subject turn has `innocent_explanation_offered`
subchecks.text: Tests offered explanations. N/A unless a subject turn has `innocent_explanation_offered`. Each innocent explanation is followed within the next three questions by a question seeking a checkable detail that could corroborate or refute it.
Discriminating question. At least one question seeks a detail whose answer would differ between the innocent and the culpable account of the key event.
No premature conclusion. No question asserts or presupposes guilt or innocence before closure.

anchors_0_to_4: No finding, or a confident finding with no content basis.
A finding with a citation but resting on how the subject came across.
A finding with citations that only partly support it.
Supported and cited, with one weakness, for example confidence one step too strong.
"Insufficient evidence, roughly even chance: turn 4 conflicts with the panel log; verify the Lab C panel log and the work-order system."
dimensions.name: supported closure

subchecks.text: Committed and cited. A finding in the allowed form exists and its stored `cited_turns` or `cited_records` is non-empty: the finding's own citations, adverse or corroborating, plus those of its basis flags (1.3.1, S2 4.8).

Citations hold. N/A unless 5a found citations. Every citation exists (code: S2 4.4.1 `finding_citation_ok`, a committed non-partial answer, or an initial document or released record) and supports the finding as its label and rationale state it (referee: `citations[].supports_basis`).
Content basis. The basis (`rationale`) rests on content (statement-evidence inconsistency, contradiction, corroboration), not on demeanor, style or evasive wording alone (EX-4).
Calibrated confidence. The likelihood term and analytic confidence respect the ceiling table below.
Names corroboration. N/A unless the label is `insufficient_evidence`. At least one `corroboration_needed` entry names a specific record, person or timeline check.
